filename: Improving extreme precipitation representation with machine learning-based warm rain microphysics in CESM._
title: Improving Extreme Precipitation Representation with ML Based Warm Rain Microphysics in CAM6
parameterization_target: warm rain microphysics (autoconversion and accretion tendencies, TAU-ML emulator replacing KK2000)
testbed_rationale: Presentation slides without links to access the underlying simulation data or model code.
pain_points: Structural error within the model revealed during history matching
Bin microphysics schemes are 30-300x too slow to run directly in Earth system models
Underestimation of extreme precipitation upper tails remains even with TAU-ML
Strong parameter sensitivity and coupling interactions with deep convection schemes (e.g., Zhang-McFarlane parameter interactions)
extraction_notes: The document is a slide presentation describing the TAU-ML warm rain microphysics emulator integrated into CAM6/CESM, paired with perturbed parameter ensembles (PPE) and history matching for auto-calibration.
